subject: SEM with random parameters and triangular distribution

messages.author: 116ad1c0bd4c1bd3
messages.subject: SEM with random parameters and triangular distribution
parts:
Hi, I am estimating a SEM with the package lavaan, but as a new user, I have the following questions:

- is it correct to factor Lickert scale variables before specifying them as latent variables? I used:
"df$lower_consum<-factor(df$lower_consum)
levels(df$lower_consum) <- c("strongly disagree", "disagree", "neutral", "agree", "strongly agree")"

- then, I would implement random parameters in the regression model. The option "fixed.x = FALSE" doesn't work. Indeed, I get the error message "fixed.x = FALSE" is not supported when conditional.x = TRUE. Any suggestion to have random instead of fixed parameters?

- Finally, I would also implement a triangular distribution for the parameters, thus avoiding long tails. I tried "int.ov.free = FALSE". It works, but is it the correct option for changing the distribution or do other options exist?

I am attaching the code for better clarity: 

df <-as.data.frame(df)

df$lower_consum<-factor(df$lower_consum)
levels(df$lower_consum) <- c("strongly disagree", "disagree", "neutral", "agree", "strongly agree")

df$env_cert_prod<-factor(df$env_cert_prod)
levels(df$env_cert_prod) <- c("strongly disagree", "disagree", "neutral", "agree", "strongly agree")

[...]

### Rename colums
colnames(df)[colnames(df) == "lower_consum"] = "soc1"
colnames(df)[colnames(df) == "env_cert_prod"] = "self1
 
[...]

### Latent variable definition
model.1 <- '
            soc =~ soc1 + soc2 + soc3
            self =~ self1 + self2 + self3

### Regression
           WTP_dummy ~ euro + gender + books +  stationery_items + return_freq + recycled_items  + feel_green_prod + feel_green_courier + soc + self
'

fit.1 <- sem(model.1, data = df, ordered = TRUE, int.ov.free = FALSE, fixed.x = FALSE, estimator = "WLS")

summary(fit.1, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)
